newsitem.title: FRANCE: IMF sees French 1997 growth at 2.4 pct in 1997.
newsitem.headline: IMF sees French 1997 growth at 2.4 pct in 1997.

text.p: The French economy should grow 2.4 percent in 1997 and 3.0 percent in 1998, the International Montetary Fund said in a report released on Wednesday.
The French government has forecast the economy will grow by a minimum 2.3 percent in 1997 and 2.8 percent in 1998.

The IMF said it believed France needed to implement extra measures to bring its government deficit durably below three percent of gross domestic product. Three percent is the target limit for European economic and monetary union.

"Fiscal plans for 1997 entail keeping central government spending unchanged in nominal terms and strict limits on social security expenditure but additional measures appear necessary to bring the deficit below three percent of GDP on a durable basis," it said.
The IMF said 1997 growth would be helped by an underlying expansion of private consumption and increase in exports.
The agency said, however, that while the business climate had improved somewhat, consumer confidence was still weak and the "projected pick-up in business investment appeared fragile".

Moreover, the IMF said in its semi-annual World Economic Outlook, it remained necessary to implement more comprehensive labour market, tax and public sector reforms to promote job creation and entrepreneurship.
It said a fall in interest rates should help recovery gain some momentum in France and Germany, but it was too early to say that the process of monetary easing had "fully run" its course.
It said French unemployment could exceed 13 percent by mid-year, up from 12.8 percent currently, and saw a risk the rising French jobless toll could weaken consumption.

"Though (economic) growth could be stronger if exchange rates remain near their levels in early 1997, there is at least an equal risk that rising unemployment could undermine consumption and that sluggishness in European growth could hinder the expansion of exports," it said.
It said that French inflationary pressures were likely to remain negligible.
